title: introduce-slo-grace-mapper-and-deferred-connection-clipper
author: Evan Chen
release_notes: Adds SLO grace mapping for per-tenant soft windows and a deferred connection clipper to prevent KV pressure cascades; includes observability and rollout flags. Backwards compatible; safe rollout via feature flag.
description:
Context: During a recent tenant surge we observed premature circuit flips caused by uniform SLO windows and a spike in long-lived inflight connections that amplified KV cache pressure. This PR adds two coordinated mechanisms: (1) a SLO Grace Mapper that translates global SLI windows into per-tenant soft-grace allowances based on recent error/latency histograms and tenant weight, and (2) a Deferred Connection Clipper which caps new long-lived connection admits when KV memory pressure or slot exhaustion is detected, releasing a small, telemetry-anchored fast-eviction path for idle connections. Goals: reduce noisy circuit flips, avoid regional chain-retries, and give high-impact tenants bounded soft slack to absorb short surges without full fallback.

What I changed (high level):
- runtime/slo_grace_mapper.go: new component that computes per-tenant "grace_seconds" and a short-term SLO slack multiplier using a rolling SLI window and tenant-weight heuristic.
- controlplane/connection_clipper.go: deferred admission controller that clips admits for connections with large KV footprints; integrates with runtime health signals and exposes clip events to tracing.
- runtime/eviction_fastpath.go: small fast-evict hook that can remove idle connections with a conservative scoring function to free KV / slot resources.
- telemetry/metrics.yml and telemetry/alerts.yml: new metrics (redwood.slo_grace_seconds, redwood.conn_clip_events, redwood.fast_evict_rate) and an alert to detect miscalibration of grace mappings.
- config/feature_flags.yaml: feature flag and rollout ramps (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with per-cluster opt-out.
- tests/*: unit + deterministic integration tests for mapper heuristics and clipper state machine; added e2e scenario that simulates a KV-pressure surge and validates graceful degradation behavior.

Migration and rollout notes: feature-guarded behind feature/slo-grace and feature/conn-clipper flags. Default flags off for dedicated/private deployments; enabled in canary for 10% of hostnames for 24h, then 50% after telemetry sanity. No DB migrations. Backstop: if clipper misbehaves, flip feature flags to fully disable fast-evict and the mapper falls back to prior static windows.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for SLO mapper heuristics
- [x] Integration test simulating KV pressure
- [x] Metrics and dashboards added
- [x] Feature flags added for staged rollout
- [x] Docs: short runbook section added to ops guide

Related: ENG-9876 (slo-smoothing initiative), SUP-331 (incident traced to region-eu-2), ENG-9921 (telemetry-driven rollouts).

review_comments: Marisol Rivera (reviewer): Nice isolation between mapper and clipper. Concern: mapper has heuristic multipliers that could be gamed by bursty tenants—please add a monotonic cap and document the cap rationale.
Evan Chen (author): Added a monotonic cap (maxGraceSeconds = 30s) and documented reasoning in code comments and runbook. See updated tests that assert cap enforcement.

Priya Kumar (reviewer): CI flakes in integration test  TestKVPressureSim once seen — looks related to clipper shutdown race. Can you ensure clipper drains pending timers on stop? Also add a test for a negative edge case when health signals are delayed.
Evan Chen (author): Fixed shutdown race by joining the timer goroutine and added TestClipperDelayedHealthSignal to the integration harness. Re-ran CI locally and reproduced failing case before fix.

Logan Brooks (reviewer): Telemetry names look good. Request: add a percentile-based alert check instead of a raw rate to avoid alert storms during rollout. Also confirm metric cardinality won't explode per-tenant.
Evan Chen (author): Switched the alert to use 99th percentile over 5m for redwood.conn_clip_events and added explicit cardinality bucketing to metrics.yml (tenant bucket: topN + "other").
